best_parts: node a_t9: names the tempting model (indirect is the commonest inguinal type), refutes it with the 'groin versus inguinal' scope word, and pairs it with a sure_note on the same error
node a_ok / a_probe skip option ('Skip the mechanism, straight to a case' to f_probe): a real fast lane that still reaches every core objective
nodes e1_probe to e2_ok: eponym matching anchored to the site (inguinal versus femoral sac), with a cold, hint-free final probe in the same segment
flaws: node a_probe: the key 'Femoral hernia, below the ligament' is the only option with a positional qualifier and the longest label, so it is findable by form (DP1)
node c1_t5b: 'Inguinal hernia, as a group' tempts almost no one with surface knowledge, so it is dominated (DP2)
node b_probe: the key 'A narrow neck at the deep ring grips the contents' is again the longest option; the mechanism probe telegraphs

best_parts: node groin_contrast and gc_t_pan: the 'groin' stem is re-tested with femoral removed, and the pantaloon distractor is tied to bulk as the wrong model
node g_vig: a tender, irreducible lump located below and lateral to the tubercle, with each wrong option mapped to a distinct wrong model (TR9 or TR8)
node fc_ok and f_contrast: the 'relatively commoner' qualifier is separated from 'most common', with the feedback naming the comparison versus ranking distinction
flaws: node groin_probe: the key 'Femoral hernia, below the inguinal ligament' is the longest label and the only one that adds a positional clause, so the key is findable by form (DP1); the same pattern repeats at gc_ok, neck_ok and e_ok

nodes groin_t8, groin_t9, gv_t9, e_t11 and the other trap feedback: the only exit is 'Try again'. A learner who misses twice never reaches the explanation of the key, so the hint ladder stops at a hint (pedagogy: a second miss must get the explanation)
node fc_t_b: 'Inguinal hernia is much commoner in women than in men' is dominated, since it contradicts the sex comparison most learners already hold (DP2)

best_parts: node scope_t9 and pair_t9: the scope-word trap is shown as a same-question, two-wording contrast (groin versus inguinal), which is a different technique from the single-stem probe and tests the same error in a new form
nodes worked, mistake, mistake_ok, why: a worked case followed by an error-spotting probe (which step is the mistake?), so the learner generates the reason taxis is dangerous rather than being told
node recap: the device 'neck, scope, site' gives the learner three handles that map onto the segment's three error families
flaws: node mistake: the distractor 'Diagnosing it as a femoral hernia' is not a wrong model. Its own feedback says the diagnosis is right, so it is a non-trap labelled TR9 and it lets the learner eliminate the option by a second reason (DP2, R2)
node pct and m5: 'Direct inguinal hernia is the commonest type in women' is dominated, since no one with the wrong model 'femoral is commoner in women' would pick direct; it diagnoses nothing

node neck: the stem asserts the fact ('Indirect hernias are more liable to strangulate. Why?'), so the learner is told the claim before committing to it (R1); the segment also has no fast lane for experts

merge_ideas: a's skip lane and 'Show me the answer' exit on every trap, with c's worked-case error-spotting probe placed before the scope stem, so the expert skips and the novice gets a worked example
c's A/B same-question contrast for the scope word, with a's sure_note on each trap, so the high-confidence error is corrected in a form the learner has not yet seen
b's 'relatively' versus 'most common' contrast (f_contrast) added to c's sex-skew section, replacing c's dominated direct-hernia distractor
a single length-matched label style across all keys (no key longer or shorter than its distractors), taken from a's e1/e2 eponym options
